dedupe_keys.name: us environmentally extended input output useeio models

description: USEEIO is a family of combined economic and environmental input-output models of the U.S. economy, developed by EPA researchers for the sustainable materials management programme. The models pair Bureau of Economic Analysis input-output tables on transactions among 389 industry sectors, final consumption and value added with satellite tables of land, water, energy and mineral use, air pollution, nutrients and toxics, and with indicators of environmental and economic impact, using standard input-output algorithms. They are used by EPA offices, other agencies, companies, NGOs and academia for carbon footprints and environmental assessments, and underpin EPA's Sustainable Materials Management Prioritization Tools and the Recycling Economic Information report. State models (USEEIO State Models v1.0, 2024) and a version 2.0 national model (Scientific Data, 2022) are documented. Data products are free on data.gov (search useeio), the source code is in the USEEIO Modeling Framework, and versions are listed in the project's models file. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): EPA web policy: EPA-produced content is in the public domain unless otherwise specified (software licence not stated separately). Caveats: the models are static and national or state-level, with sector detail limited to the BEA classification. For simulation it gives the U.S. inter-industry network with environmental extensions for supply-chain and impact analyses. Related catalogue records include FLOWSA and pymrio.
